The University of Lahore — Academic Affairs Directorate
1. ACADEMIC YEAR STRUCTURE & GOVERNANCE
The University of Lahore operates on a semester system comprising two regular 16-week semesters (Fall and
Spring) and an optional 8-week Summer session dedicated to deficiency clearance, course repetition, and
accelerated learning modules. The Academic Affairs Directorate prepares and regulates the official university
calendar approved by the Academic Council.

Spring Semester: Instructional period spanning February through May, followed by terminal

The University of Lahore — General Admissions Directorate
1. GENERAL INSTITUTIONAL INTRODUCTION & FRAMEWORK
The University of Lahore maintains rigorous academic standards across its diverse faculties, including
Engineering, Computer Science, Medical Sciences, Management Sciences, Social Sciences, and Law. The
admissions policy is designed to select candidates who demonstrate exceptional academic capability,
intellectual curiosity, and potential for leadership. Admissions are awarded purely on a competitive merit basis
in accordance with the regulatory standards established by national accreditation bodies including the Higher

Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC), Pakistan Medical & Dental Council
(PMDC), and Pakistan Bar Council (PBC).
This comprehensive guidelines manual establishes the governing principles, minimum entry qualifications,
verification protocols, fee payment schedules, and enrollment workflows applicable to all prospective
undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral applicants seeking admission for the upcoming academic session.

1.1 Scope & Applicability of Policies
These guidelines apply to all campus locations, constituent colleges, and affiliated institutes under the
governance of the University of Lahore. Every candidate registering on the official university portal is legally
bound to adhere to the terms, dates, and documentation requirements set forth herein. Failure to satisfy any
statutory requirement or presenting false documentation at any stage will lead to immediate cancellation of
admission and forfeiture of fees paid.

2. UNDERGRADUATE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA & SUBJECT PREREQUISITES
Applicants applying for undergraduate degree programs must have completed 12 years of formal education or
an equivalent foreign qualification recognized by the Inter Board Committee of Chairmen (IBCC).
2.1 Secondary & Higher Secondary Qualification Benchmarks
Faculty of Engineering & Technology: Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) Pre-Engineering or
equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, achieving an overall aggregate of at least 60%
unadjusted marks. Candidates holding a 3-year Diploma of Associate Engineer (DAE) in a relevant

gregate of at least 60%
unadjusted marks. Candidates holding a 3-year Diploma of Associate Engineer (DAE) in a relevant
technological discipline with 60% marks are eligible against designated diploma seats.
Faculty of Computer Science & Information Technology: HSSC in Pre-Engineering, Pre-Medical, or
Computer Science (ICS) with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks. Candidates with Pre-Medical
background must successfully complete two deficiency courses in Mathematics during their first year of
study.

category:

Engineering Discipline Formula: Aggregate % = (SSC % × 0.10) + (HSSC Pre-Eng % × 0.40) + (Entry
Test % × 0.50)
Postgraduate Research Formula: Aggregate % = (BS Academic Percentage × 0.40) + (GAT/UGET Test

EXAMINATION RULES & ASSESSMENT POLICIES
The University of Lahore — Controller of Examinations Directorate
1. ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK & EV ALUATION SYSTEMS
The Controller of Examinations Directorate is responsible for maintaining the validity, academic integrity,
secrecy, and rigorous standards of all continuous assessments, mid-term evaluations, practical performance
exams, and terminal semester examinations across all academic faculties.
This manual defines assessment structures, eligibility benchmarks, grading scales, GPA/CGPA calculation
models, attendance thresholds, re-examination rules, and disciplinary procedures concerning academic
misconduct.
1.1 Continuous Assessment Composition

re-examination rules, and disciplinary procedures concerning academic
misconduct.
1.1 Continuous Assessment Composition
The academic performance of students in each course is evaluated through a combination of continuous
formative assessments and summative terminal examinations:
Quizzes, Class Tests & Assignments: 15% to 20% of total course marks.
Mid-Term Written Examination: 25% to 30% of total course marks, administered at the middle of the
semester (Week 8).
Laboratory Practical / Project Work / Case Studies: 10% to 15% (for courses with embedded
practical components).
Final Terminal Examination: 40% to 50% of total course marks, held at the conclusion of the 16-week
instructional term.

Final Terminal Examination: 40% to 50% of total course marks, held at the conclusion of the 16-week
instructional term.
2. EXAMINATION ELIGIBILITY & ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENTS
Admission to examination halls for both mid-term and final examinations is conditional upon satisfying strict
academic and administrative criteria.
2.1 Mandatory Eligibility Criteria
75% Class Attendance Rule: Students must maintain a minimum cumulative attendance of 75% in
lecture hours and practical laboratory sessions scheduled for each course.
Financial Clearance: Zero outstanding balance on student finance accounts prior to exam roll number
allocation.

3.2 Calculation Formulas for GPA and CGPA
Grade Point Average (GPA): Calculated at the conclusion of each semester by dividing total quality points
earned by total credit hours attempted during that specific semester.
Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA): Calculated by dividing total cumulative quality points earned
across all semesters by total cumulative credit hours completed.
4. RE-EXAMINATION, MAKE-UP TESTS & COURSE REPEATS
Academic progression guidelines define exact parameters under which re-examinations, make-up tests, and
course repeats are permitted.
4.1 Special Make-Up Examinations
Make-up examinations for mid-term or final terminal exams are granted only under extraordinary

ial Make-Up Examinations
Make-up examinations for mid-term or final terminal exams are granted only under extraordinary
circumstances such as hospitalization, severe medical emergency, or official representation of the university
in national sports/academic events.
Application Timeline: The student must submit a formal application along with authenticated medical
proof (certified by a recognized hospital) within 3 working days of the missed examination.
Sanctioning Body: All make-up requests are evaluated by the University Medical Board and approved
by the Controller of Examinations.

4.2 Course Repeat for Grade Improvement
Undergraduate students obtaining a grade of 'D' or 'F' may re-register for the course during regular semesters
or summer terms. The higher grade earned will replace the original grade in CGPA calculation, though the
original grade will remain recorded on the historical transcript transcript log.

fair defense for accused students.

Communicating written decisions within 14 days of the hearing.

7. FEE REVISION POLICIES & ANNUAL ESCALATION RATES
Tuition rates and administrative fees are subject to periodic review by the Board of Governors to account for
inflation, laboratory equipment upgrades, and operational overheads.

Annual tuition fees for continuing students may be revised by a maximum of 5% to 8% at the
commencement of each academic year. Notice of fee revisions is published on the student portal at least 60
days prior to the start of the Fall semester.

4. SPECIAL CATEGORY WAIVERS & CONCESSIONS
The university maintains specialized tuition waivers to support specific student categories and promote social
inclusivity.
4.1 Kinship Concession
A 25% tuition fee concession is awarded to the second biological sibling actively enrolled in a full-time
degree program at the university. If three siblings are enrolled simultaneously, the third sibling receives a
50% tuition waiver.
4.2 Sports & Co-Curricular Talent Scholarships
National Level Athletes: Up to 100% tuition waiver for players representing national teams in
recognized sports.
Provincial / University Representation: 25% to 50% waiver subject to performance trial evaluation by

recognized sports.

the University Sports Board.
4.3 University Employees & Alumni Child Concession
Children and spouses of full-time permanent university staff and faculty members receive a 50% tuition fee
waiver, while children of registered alumni receive a 15% tuition concession.

Regular lecture presence and active participation in tutorial sessions are fundamental requirements for
academic progression.
2.1 Attendance Rules & Disqualification Thresholds
Course instructors record attendance digitally at the start of each lecture session. Students must achieve a
minimum of 75% attendance in every course to qualify for final examinations.
Punctuality Rule: Students are required to be seated in lecture halls prior to the scheduled class time.

require a verified hospital medical certificate.

during academic evaluations.

All research reports, term papers, thesis drafts, and assignments must be processed through Turnitin
plagiarism detection software. In accordance with Higher Education Commission guidelines, any document
exhibiting a similarity index exceeding 19% (or direct copying exceeding 5% from a single source) will be
rejected.

members.

Prohibition of Narcotics, Tobacco & Vaping: The university campus is a designated zero-tolerance
smoke-free and drug-free facility. Possession, consumption, or distribution of cigarettes, electronic vapes,
or illegal substances results in immediate expulsion and legal referral.
Anti-Ragging Regulations: Physical or psychological harassment, ragging, or coercion of junior
students is strictly banned.

i-Ragging Regulations: Physical or psychological harassment, ragging, or coercion of junior
students is strictly banned. Violators face immediate suspension, heavy fines, and expulsion.
Political & Sectarian Activity Ban: Students are strictly prohibited from forming political unions,
organizing unauthorized rallies, distributing political literature, or inviting external political speakers on
campus.

4.2 Traffic, Parking & Vehicle Access Regulations
All student vehicles entering campus must display a valid University Parking Sticker issued by the Campus
Security Office. Vehicles must park strictly in designated student parking zones. Speed limits on campus
roadways are restricted to 20 km/h.

decisions fairly.

If unaddressed within 5 working days, the grievance is escalated to the University Student Grievance

Student Counselor.

A student penalized by the Campus Disciplinary Committee has the right to lodge a final appeal to the Vice-
Chancellor within 14 calendar days of decision notification. The decision of the Vice-Chancellor acting as
Appellate Authority is final and binding.

7.1 Hostel Entry Rules & Curfew Timings
Hostel residents must adhere strictly to residential decorum and curfew hours. Female hostels observe a strict
entry curfew of 8:00 PM in summer and 7:00 PM in winter. Overnight stay outside hostels requires prior
written consent from parents and warden authorization.

Hostel mess committees comprising student representatives inspect food quality, kitchen hygiene, and menu
planning weekly. Cooking in individual hostel rooms is strictly prohibited.
